tagline: Latin America's leading beverage company with diversified portfolio in beer, wine, and non-alcoholic drinks
hero_kpi_rationale: EBITDA margin is CCU's key KPI, reflecting operational profitability and the company's ability to manage costs and pricing despite a challenging macroeconomic environment (devaluations, inflation in Argentina, commodity volatility). It demonstrates the group's operational resilience.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue remaining after deducting direct production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved by 55 basis points as a percentage of sales, driven by the appreciation of the Chilean peso against the dollar and efficiency gains, despite rising aluminum costs.
kpis.signal: Gross margin improved slightly despite cost pressures from aluminum and currency headwinds

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a measure of core profitability.
kpis.description: EBITDA remained nearly stable thanks to strong performance in Chile (+13.7%), offsetting declines in International America (-18.6%) and Wine (-50.1%).
kpis.signal: EBITDA remained stable despite strong Chilean performance offsetting international headwinds

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated by the company.
kpis.description: Sales growth was nearly flat (+0.2%) despite a 1.8% increase in volumes, due to a 1.5% decline in average prices in Chilean pesos, affected by ARS depreciation against the USD.
kpis.signal: Revenue growth modest due to pricing pressure offset by volume gains in Chile

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income declined by 6.8% to CLP 53.9 billion, primarily due to margin contraction in the international and wine segments.
kpis.signal: Net income declined despite operational stability due to international segment and wine margin compression

kpis.name: Consolidated Volumes
kpis.explanation: Total quantity of products sold by the company in billions of units.
kpis.description: Consolidated volumes increased by 1.8%, driven by a 3.9% expansion in Chile, despite declines in International America (-1.7%) and Wine (-5.9%).
kpis.signal: Volume growth driven by strong Chilean performance offsetting international weakness

kpis.name: EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: EBITDA expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: EBITDA margin remained unchanged at 16.1%, reflecting balanced management of growth, costs, and pricing amid commodity volatility and exchange rate fluctuations.
kpis.signal: EBITDA margin resilient at 16.1% despite commodity volatility and currency headwinds

risks.title: Dependence on brand licensing agreements
risks.summary: Expiration or termination of licensing agreements could affect certain operational segments. Although CCU has reduced this exposure (70% owned brands by 2025), loss of major licenses (e.g., international brands) could impact revenues and competitiveness.
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly identified in A.1 with moderate language ('could negatively impact'). CCU operates under licenses with specific conditions; however, 70% of sales come from owned brands by 2025, mitigating impact. Trend stable. Medium category weight for beverage sector.

risks.title: Volatility in raw material and input costs
risks.summary: CCU depends on volatile raw materials (malt, sugar, fruit pulp, hops, concentrates) and packaging exposed to exchange rate, climate, and geopolitical conflict fluctuations. Chile's PUSU law mandates 15% local recycled plastic (2025-2030), increasing costs if local supply is insufficient.
risks.score_rationale: Risk detailed in A.2 with strong language ('exposed to market volatility', 'variables which the Company has no control over'). Multiple factors: exchange rates, climate, geopolitics. Linked to PUSU (15% recycled plastic mandate 2025-2030). Trend up (inflationary pressure 2022-2025). Very high category weight for beverage producer.

risks.title: Shortage of critical raw materials and inputs
risks.summary: Changes in consumption, agricultural fluctuations, logistics issues, and regulatory constraints (PUSU) could reduce the availability of critical raw materials, affecting production levels and CCU's competitive position.
risks.score_rationale: Autonomous risk in A.3 with direct language ('eventual shortage', 'could affect the Company's supply chain'). Multiple causes: consumption shifts, agricultural production, quality/availability, logistics. Explicit link to PUSU. Trend up (post-COVID supply chain tensions). Critical category weight for production.

risks.title: Geographic concentration: dependence on Chile and Argentina
risks.summary: CCU generates 91% of revenues in Chile and Argentina, exposed to recessions, high inflation (12.8% in Chile in 2022), currency devaluations, price and exchange controls, and regulatory instability. Argentina has remained hyperinflationary since 2018 with risk of new restrictions.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk in A.4 with detailed exposure: Chile 64% of revenues, Argentina 27% (International segment). Strong language on macroeconomic volatility, inflation (12.8% in 2022), exchange controls (2019-2023), price controls (2020-2023). Argentina hyperinflationary since 2018. Trend stable but fragile context. Very high category weight.

risks.title: Antitrust risks and abuse of dominant position
risks.summary: CCU, market leader in Chile, faces a lawsuit for abuse of dominant position before the Tribunal for the Defense of Free Competition (TDLC) and commitments to the National Economic Prosecutor (FNE) regarding anti-competitive practices. An adverse ruling could result in financial penalties and reputational damage.
risks.score_rationale: Risk detailed in B.1 with concrete cases: ongoing lawsuit in Chile for abuse of dominant position in on-premise beer market; FNE commitment on anti-competitive practices (microbreweries). Moderate language but explicit financial/reputational risks. Trend stable. High category weight for market leader.

risks.title: Regulatory changes in labeling and advertising
risks.summary: Labeling and advertising regulations are constantly evolving in CCU's markets. Chilean Law 21,363 imposes alcohol warnings, time restrictions, and advertising limitations at sporting events, potentially reducing consumption and impacting marketing strategy.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified in B.3 with concrete example: Chilean Law 21,363 (alcohol advertising restrictions, warnings, time/event limitations). Moderate language ('constantly changing', 'could impact'). Trend up (increasing health/wellness regulation). Medium category weight for alcohol/beverage sector.

risks.title: Changing lifestyles and consumption preferences
risks.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic and other events have accelerated lifestyle changes: competition from digital entertainment, safety concerns, and health/wellness trends are reducing consumption occasions. CCU must innovate to adapt its multi-category portfolio to these shifts.
risks.score_rationale: Structural risk in A.6 with nuanced language ('some structural, others transitory'). Causes: COVID-19, digital entertainment, individualism, citizen security, health/wellness trends. CCU acknowledges innovation capacity but risk of disruption. Trend up (post-COVID acceleration). High category weight for beverages.

risks.title: Retention of key talent and operational continuity
risks.summary: The departure or high turnover of key employees could affect operational continuity, strategic execution, and CCU's innovation capacity, weakening its competitiveness.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified in A.5 with moderate language ('could negatively affect'). Impacts: operational continuity, strategic execution, innovation, knowledge loss. No specific turnover data. Trend stable. Medium category weight for manufacturing sector.
